facts.statement: A female ensign wasp uses a slender egg-laying organ called an ovipositor to place one egg inside a tough cockroach egg case. American cockroaches are among its documented hosts.
facts.quote: slender ovipositor into the tough ootheca

facts.statement: The developing wasp larva feeds on the dozen or more cockroach eggs inside that case. An egg case successfully consumed in this way will not produce cockroaches.
The ensign wasp described in this article does not sting or bite people.
The adult ensign wasp described is 5-7 mm long. Its stalked abdomen resembles a small signal flag and is waved up and down, giving the wasp its name.
